correctness.rationale: The published odd-prime monomial representations have degree phi(p^k), diagonal a-action through a primitive p^k root, and cyclic-shift b-action whose d_k-th power is omega I. If a^x b^y is in the kernel, the permutation part forces d_k|y; comparison of two diagonal entries forces p^k|x because p does not divide r-1; the remaining scalar condition is omega^(y/d_k)=1. This gives kernel size p^(2(n-k)-s), codegree p^(k+s), and the exact nonlinear multiplicity p^(t-1) at p^t. Adding cyclic-quotient linear characters gives the displayed formula. The checker verifies the parameter enumeration and degree-squared identity.

value.rationale: Cyclic prime-power holomorphs are a classical metacyclic family with a complete published representation parametrization, making them a natural test case for the newer pseudo-algebra invariant. The theorem gives the entire codegree distribution, not a single statistic, and shows that the invariant recovers both structural parameters p and n. The n>=2 result also exhibits how the new p-part of the automorphism group changes the invariant beyond the already-understood affine n=1 boundary.
